_comment: Copy to ~/.config/htpc-remote/devices.json and chmod 600 — it holds secrets.
Override the location with the HTPC_REMOTE_DEVICES environment variable.
You normally do NOT need to write this by hand. Open Glide on your phone,
tap the gear in the device tab strip, and follow the Setup screen — it
scans your LAN, reads your Tuya account, and writes this file for you.
Getting the values manually, if you prefer:
1. pip install tinytuya && python -m tinytuya wizard
(needs a free iot.tuya.com cloud project linked to your Smart Life
account; see the wiki page 'TV and IR Control')
2. The wizard writes devices.json — take 'key' as local_key, plus the
hub id and the per-TV remote id it lists.
Transports, tried in order:
local — replays a stored base64 code over the LAN. ~20ms, works with no
internet. Used only for actions that actually have a stored code.
cloud — fires keys from the codeset Smart Life already configured.
~200-500ms, needs internet and a live IoT Core subscription.
Populate the local codes either by teaching them from a physical remote
(Teach button) or, if your hub can't report captures, with the one-tap
'Load LG' button which synthesises them from published NEC values.
local_control defaults to true and is safe to leave on: local sending is
only used for actions that have a stored code, and a hub that cannot send
locally never accumulates any, so everything falls back to the cloud.
Set it to false only if you want to force cloud-only.
